claim: Adult-born granule cells (ABGCs) are involved in certain forms of hippocampus-dependent learning and memory.
source: Adult-born granule cells (ABGCs) are involved in certain forms of hippocampus-dependent learning and memory.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature establishing this relationship.

claim: Young but functionally integrated ABGCs (4-weeks-old) specifically contribute to pattern separation functions of the dentate gyrus due to their heightened excitability.
source: It has been proposed that young but functionally integrated ABGCs (4-weeks-old) specifically contribute to pattern separation functions of the dentate gyrus due to their heightened excitability, whereas old ABGCs (>8 weeks old) lose these capabilities.
evidence: This is a statement of what has been proposed in the field, supported by the literature context.

claim: Old ABGCs (>8 weeks old) lose pattern separation capabilities.
source: It has been proposed that young but functionally integrated ABGCs (4-weeks-old) specifically contribute to pattern separation functions of the dentate gyrus due to their heightened excitability, whereas old ABGCs (>8 weeks old) lose these capabilities.
evidence: This is a statement of what has been proposed in the field, supported by the literature context.

claim: ABGCs consist of two functionally distinguishable populations showing highly distinct input integration properties.
source: Measuring multiple cellular and integrative characteristics of 3- 10-week-old individual ABGCs, we show that ABGCs consist of two functionally distinguishable populations showing highly distinct input integration properties (one group being highly sensitive to narrow input intensity ranges while the other group linearly reports input strength) that are largely independent of the cellular age and maturation stage
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental measurements of cellular and integrative characteristics presented in the manuscript.

claim: One ABGC group is highly sensitive to narrow input intensity ranges while the other group linearly reports input strength.
source: Measuring multiple cellular and integrative characteristics of 3- 10-week-old individual ABGCs, we show that ABGCs consist of two functionally distinguishable populations showing highly distinct input integration properties (one group being highly sensitive to narrow input intensity ranges while the other group linearly reports input strength)
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data on input-output functions of individual ABGCs.

claim: The two functionally distinct ABGC populations are largely independent of cellular age and maturation stage.
source: that are largely independent of the cellular age and maturation stage, suggesting that 'classmate' cells (born during the same period) can contribute to the network with fundamentally different functions.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing functional separation independent of age.

claim: 'Classmate' cells (born during the same period) can contribute to the network with fundamentally different functions.
source: suggesting that 'classmate' cells (born during the same period) can contribute to the network with fundamentally different functions.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation that functional properties are independent of cellular age.

claim: ABGCs provide two temporally overlapping but functionally distinct neuronal cell populations.
source: Thus, ABGCs provide two temporally overlapping but functionally distinct neuronal cell populations, adding a novel level of complexity to our understanding of how life-long neurogenesis contributes to adult brain function.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the experimental findings presented in the manuscript.

claim: Adult neurogenesis contributes to certain forms of hippocampus-dependent behavior.
source: Adult neurogenesis contributes to certain forms of hippocampus-dependent behavior and is associated with a number of neuro-psychiatric diseases (Parent and Murphy, 2008; Deng et al., 2010; Kheirbek et al., 2012; Spalding et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: Adult neurogenesis is associated with a number of neuro-psychiatric diseases.

claim: Young ABGCs (around 4 weeks old) contribute to a discrete pattern separation function.
source: Recent data suggested that young ABGCs (around 4 weeks old) contribute to a discrete pattern separation function, whereas older cells (8 weeks or older) are not necessary for this dentate gyrus-dependent function, therefore functionally different pools of granule cells provide unique plasticity to the hippocampal circuits (Clelland et al., 2009; Aimone et al., 2010; Alme et al., 2010; Sahay et al., 2011a; Nakashiba et al., 2012; Neunuebel and Knierim, 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: Older ABGCs (8 weeks or older) are not necessary for pattern separation function.
source: Recent data suggested that young ABGCs (around 4 weeks old) contribute to a discrete pattern separation function, whereas older cells (8 weeks or older) are not necessary for this dentate gyrus-dependent function, therefore functionally different pools of granule cells provide unique plasticity to the hippocampal circuits (Clelland et al., 2009; Aimone et al., 2010; Alme et al., 2010; Sahay et al., 2011a; Nakashiba et al., 2012; Neunuebel and Knierim, 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: Functionally different pools of granule cells provide unique plasticity to the hippocampal circuits.

claim: Current theories on adult neurogenesis are based on provisional correlations between two distinct physiological functions and age-dependent maturation of cellular properties.

claim: ABGCs acquire neuronal properties including synaptic inputs and outputs, and capability of firing action potentials 3 to 4 weeks after their birth.

evidence: This claim is supported by established knowledge in the field.

claim: Retroviral labeling was used for birth-dating of ABGCs.
source: To analyze the cellular maturation of ABGCs, we compared a variety of intrinsic biophysical and input–output transformation properties at seven different age-groups (3–10 weeks after cells are born) of individual birth-dated ABGCs in young adult rats using retroviral labeling (Figure 2, Zhao et al., 2006).
evidence: This describes the experimental method used.

claim: 31- to 33-day-old male Wistar rats were injected with CAG-GFP or CAG-RFP Moloney murine leukemia virus vector.
source: 31- to 33-day-old male Wistar rats (95–135 g body weight) were injected with a CAG-GFP or CAG-RFP Moloney murine leukemia virus vector (Zhao et al., 2006; Jessberger et al., 2007) (0.8–1 µl) using stereotaxically targeted (5.7–5.8 mm posterior, ± 4.4–4.5 mm lateral, and 5.6–6 mm ventral from bregma), conventional Hamilton syringe under ketamine/xylazine/pipolphen anesthesia (83/17/7 mg/body kg).
evidence: This describes the experimental procedure used.

claim: Adult born granule cells were labeled along a broad longitudinal range (2–3 mm) of the hippocampi.
source: Adult born granule cells were labeled along a broad longitudinal range (2–3 mm) of the hippocampi.
evidence: This describes the experimental outcome.

claim: No cells with <3-week-old properties were found in animals 3–10 weeks after virus injection.
source: Note that we did not find cells in animals 3–10 weeks after virus injection, which had <3-week-old properties indicating the reliability and precision of the birth-dating method.
evidence: This describes an observation that validates the experimental method.

claim: Running is known to increase the number of surviving adult-born neurons.
source: After the surgical procedure two or three siblings were housed together in large cages (75 cm × 35 cm) equipped with a running wheel, toys and shelters until the electrophysiological experiments because running is known to increase the number of surviving adult-born neurons (Kempermann et al., 1997; Tashiro et al., 2007; Dranovsky et al., 2011).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Sinusoidal current injection from theta to high gamma frequency bands was used to measure input–output characteristics of ABGCs.
source: In order to measure the input–output characteristics of ABGCs during different stages of their maturation, we used sinusoidal current injection from theta to high gamma frequency bands (5, 10, 20, 40, 60, 80 Hz, 50 pA increment from the holding level of 0 pA, tested in random order) for 1 s and analyzed the number of the elicited action potentials.
evidence: This describes the experimental method used.

claim: Application of sinusoidal current injections from resting membrane potential mimicked temporally correlated excitatory drives in functionally relevant frequency ranges.
source: Application of sinusoidal current injections from resting membrane potential mimicked temporally correlated excitatory drives in functionally relevant frequency ranges, in opposed to square pulses, which would strongly recruit non-physiological mechanisms such as inactivation of voltage activated conductances.
evidence: This is a justification for the experimental approach based on physiological reasoning.

claim: The amplitude of miniature excitatory events recorded at the somata does not increase further after 3–4 weeks of ABGCs.
